commit.message:
Fix PWA offline correctness in workbox config

Three offline-from-homescreen failure modes caught by the new
@freegamestore/compliance PWA-offline check:

- Raise maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes to 10 MB so the main bundle
  is precached (default 2 MB silently drops bigger chunks).
- Add runtimeCaching for fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com
  so Google Fonts work on cold offline launch in iOS standalone.
- Extend globPatterns to wasm + json so non-default asset types
  (e.g. stockfish.wasm) get precached.

Mirrors the reference config in the bowling repo.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Bump @freegamestore/games to ^0.13.0

docs(CLAUDE): adopt slim per-repo shape

Refactors this CLAUDE.md to the slim convention documented in
SKILLS.md. Platform-wide knowledge (tech stack, brand, deploy,
mobile rules, paths) lives in SKILLS.md as the single source of
truth -- duplicating it per repo just creates drift surface area
that breaks AI agents over time. This file now only carries
what is unique to this repo.

fix(eval-bar): show "M" instead of "+999.99" when Stockfish reports mate

Stockfish returns mate as ±99999-ish centipawns. The eval bar formatter
showed that as "+999.99" / "-999.99" — technically accurate but visually
wrong. Now collapses to "+M" / "-M" when |eval| ≥ 10000.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(board): file/rank labels were unreadable — tiny + miscolored

Two bugs in the SVG board labels:

1. fontSize=13 inside an 800-wide viewBox scaled to ~540px display
   rendered as ~8.7px on screen — barely legible. Bumped to 22 (and
   weight 700, opacity 0.6) so they sit subtly in each square corner
   but are actually readable.

2. The contrast formula included `(flipped ? 1 : 0)`, which broke the
   logic: square colors at each viewBox position do NOT change when
   the board flips (only WHICH file/rank is labeled there). With the
   flipped offset, all bottom-row file labels rendered dark-on-dark
   (or light-on-light) when playing as Black — completely invisible.
   File labels also missed the +7 offset since they live in row 7.

   Removed the flipped offset; file labels use (col + 7) % 2, rank
   labels use row % 2.

3. File labels were at y=792 — bottom edge of the viewBox — and got
   clipped by the rounded corner + overflow:hidden. Moved to y=776.

Found by /qa: noticed rank labels visible but barely; file labels
invisible; same again when flipped to Black.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(rules): rewrite Game Rules panel — accurate, complete, properly formatted

Old panel was a stale inline JSX blob: said "Six difficulty levels"
(actually 5), didn't mention puzzles, listed bullets as <li> without
list styling so the SDK reset stripped them to plain text lines.

New panel:
- Three sections: Playing, Puzzles, Voice control
- Inline styles enforce list-style-disc + indentation (survives SDK reset)
- Mentions all current features incl. puzzles, click-to-see-alternative,
  voice command examples ("knight to f3", "castle kingside", etc.)
- Extracted into RulesPanel component (line 48 went from a 700-char
  inline JSX wall to <RulesPanel />)

Found by /qa: opened Game Rules modal, content was wrong + ugly.

Add SFX via SDK useGameSounds (jump / pickup / land / game-over)

The @freegamestore/games SDK exports useGameSounds(), which synthesizes
short SFX via Web Audio and automatically respects the topbar mute toggle —
so no audio files to bundle and no per-game mute plumbing.

Wired:
- playMove on jump (Space)
- playScore on gem collide
- playDrop on airborne -> grounded transition (tracked via wasGrounded flag)
- playGameOver when player falls off the bottom

Verified in browser: oscillator events fire at the expected times after
clicking the topbar Unmute, silent when muted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Polish: letterbox canvas, swap coin sprite for blue gem, bob/sway gems

- kaplay letterbox: true so the 800x600 buffer scales to fill the GameShell
  area instead of sitting top-left with a white gutter
- Coin sprite was an unreadable orange ember-blob at game-size; swap to
  tile_0067 (clean blue diamond) which reads as a valuable pickup
- Replace 180°/sec rotation (looked like a tumbling rock for a diamond
  shape) with a hover bob (4 px sine) + small ±6° sway, phase-randomized
  per gem so a row doesn't move in lockstep

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add Kenney pixel-art graphics and fix StrictMode WebGL crash

- 9 CC0 sprites under web/public/sprites/ from Kenney "Pixel Platformer"
  and "Background Elements" packs (~17 KB total, served as static assets;
  zero JS bundle impact). LICENSE.txt records attribution.
- Sprite-based player (2-frame hop animation), tiled grass-top platforms,
  spinning coin sprites
- 3-layer parallax background: distant mountains, mid + near hills,
  drifting clouds, sun with halo, sky gradient
- Defer kaplay() into a queueMicrotask so React 19 StrictMode's
  synchronous setup -> cleanup -> setup sequence doesn't quit-then-recreate
  on the same canvas (which lost the WebGL context and left the game
  loop ticking on a dead context)
- compliance test: drop unused const that was blocking tsc -b
- pnpm-lock: align with package.json's ^0.13.0 SDK pin

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Respect platform mute toggle in SoundFX

The custom Web Audio in src/sound.ts plays pin clatter, ball-roll noise,
strike/spare flourishes — all the genre-essential sounds bowling needs.
But it never read the platform mute state, so clicking the topbar Mute
button on bowling did nothing.

Fix: SoundFX gets a setMuted(boolean) method. ensureCtx() short-circuits
to null when muted, which lets every public method early-return through
the existing null-context guard with one extra line. When the toggle
flips on mid-roll, the active rolling sound is also stopped.

In Game.tsx the SDK's useSound() hook is read once at component level and
piped into the SoundFX instance via useEffect on [muted]. SoundFX defaults
to muted=true to match the SDK's "muted by default" — the very brief gap
between mount and the first sync effect can't leak a sound that way.

This unblocks the audio-mute-respect compliance check now landing in
fgs/platform.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: ignore .gstack/ in repo

Local gstack tooling drops state into .gstack/; same treatment as
.vibe-check/ so it doesn't get accidentally staged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: import shadowGeneratorSceneComponent side-effect

The Babylon deep-imports refactor in b38089a missed that ShadowGenerator
needs Lights/Shadows/shadowGeneratorSceneComponent imported as a
side-effect — without it, `new ShadowGenerator(...)` throws
"ShadowGeneratorSceneComponent needs to be imported before as it
contains a side-effect required by your code", the Game effect crashes,
React unmounts the tree, and the page renders blank.

Why no one caught it earlier:
- the build succeeds (deep imports type-check fine in isolation)
- the compliance/CI gates don't run WebGL in a real browser
- /sw.js wasn't deployed pre-this-session so the old non-PWA build was
  being served from CF, masking the bug
- once the actual deploy started running my code, the page was blank
  end-to-end

Verified the fix end-to-end with browse on http://localhost:5174 after
the dev server picked up the side-effect import: root populates with
the GameShell + lane + pins + HUD, no console errors except the
expected CORS 401 on auth.freegamestore.online/me (user not logged in).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tooling polish surfaced by a vcqa scan (vibecodeqa.online — 80→85/B):

- Biome 2.x (single-binary linter + formatter) replaces a missing
  ESLint/Prettier setup; .editorconfig for non-Biome editors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(game): rewrite for solvability, Unicode tiles, viewport scaling

The previous build was unwinnable: layout had 151 tiles (odd) and one
type had 7 copies, so pairs could never clear the board. The reverse-
construction generator was also failing silently and falling back to
random pairing every game.

- 144-tile 4-layer pyramid (88+36+16+4), all types balanced 4-of-each.
- Replace reverse-construction with greedy forward simulation: pop two
  free tiles, record the pair, repeat. The recorded sequence IS the
  solution, so the game is provably winnable by construction.
- Unicode mahjong glyphs (🀀-🀫) replace colored boxes for proper tile
  faces; white-ivory bevel + colored ink per suit (red/green/blue/dark).
- ResizeObserver + CSS transform auto-fit the board to the viewport
  (mobile-friendly).
- Remove auto-shuffle on stuck state (was an infinite useEffect loop
  on unwinnable decks); show a manual "tap Shuffle" banner instead.
- Score curve steepened: max(0, 10000 - 5·seconds).
- Delete unused Shell.tsx (orphan since SDK migration).
- New tests: 144 positions, 36×4 deck invariant, 25-seed solution replay
  that plays each generated game to completion. 27/27 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Respect platform mute toggle in playTone

playTone() created a fresh AudioContext and an oscillator every time a
color flashed during the sequence and every time the player tapped a
color — none of that read the platform mute state, so the topbar Mute
button silently did nothing on simon.

Fix: playTone now takes muted as a third arg and early-returns if true.
The component reads useSound() once, stores it in a ref so the existing
useCallback hooks (showSequence, handlePress) don't have to be recreated
on every mute toggle, and passes mutedRef.current at the two call sites.

Drive-by fixes to clear the pre-existing tsc errors that were blocking
the build:
- Add @types/node devDep so the compliance test's node:fs/node:path
  imports resolve
- Drop the unused `const css = read('src/index.css')` in compliance.test.ts
  that tripped noUnusedLocals

Fix PWA offline correctness in workbox config

Three offline-from-homescreen failure modes caught by the new
@freegamestore/compliance PWA-offline check:

- Raise maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes to 10 MB so the main bundle
  is precached (default 2 MB silently drops bigger chunks).
- Add runtimeCaching for fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com
  so Google Fonts work on cold offline launch in iOS standalone.
- Extend globPatterns to wasm + json so non-default asset types
  (e.g. stockfish.wasm) get precached.

Mirrors the reference config in the bowling repo.

Tanks: more bug fixes

- Win condition (all 5 stages cleared) now records bestScore + bestStage.
  Previously a silent miss — they only updated on the game-over path, so
  beating every stage didn't register as a high score.
- One-bullet-per-tank rule (classic Battle City). Cooldown alone wasn't
  enough — 380ms cooldown × 0.36 px/ms bullet speed = 136 px travel, far
  short of the 364px field, so rapid-tap let players have 2-3 bullets in
  flight at once. Tracking ownerId now strictly enforces the limit.
- damageBullet priority fixed: when a 4-px bullet straddles a brick + a
  steel tile, the brick was getting smashed but the outcome was reported
  as "steel" — so the smash sound + visual didn't fire. New priority is
  base > brick > steel > none.
- Steel hits now play playTick (small click) for audio feedback. Was
  silent before.

Tanks: bug fixes + visual polish

Bugs fixed
- Phase transitions (stage-clear / game-over) fired their sound + setState many
  times in a row because the if-block re-entered every animation frame between
  setPhase() and React's next render. Flip phaseRef synchronously to one-shot it.
- Player respawn placed the tank inside whatever enemy was sitting on the spawn
  point — no overlap handling. Now any overlapping enemy ram-dies (worth full
  points + popup), so the player can always emerge.
- Bullet-vs-bullet cancel — player bullets and enemy bullets now annihilate
  on collision (NES Battle City behavior). Pure pass-through was unrealistic.

Levels
- Added LEVEL_4 (steel-pillar corridors) and LEVEL_5 (steel-ring boss). Full
  5-stage progression, validated: 13 rows, all spawn zones (TL/TM/TR + player)
  clear, all 5 levels navigable with 2-wide tank.

Visuals
- Score popups (+100/+200/+400 in NES-yellow) float up from killed tanks
  and fade over 800ms.
- CRT scanline overlay across the field (1px every 3px, multiply-blended).
- Outer brown-gradient frame around the canvas with a chunky yellow border —
  closer to the NES Battle City cabinet feel.
- Drop-shadow on score-popup text for readability against any tile.

Tanks: stages + progression, tank-vs-tank collision, NES-style UI

Levels & progression
- 3 distinct stage layouts (open / brick / steel-maze) of escalating difficulty
- Stage state machine: intro → stage-intro → playing → stage-clear → next stage / over / won
- "STAGE N" overlay on entry (1.8s)
- Stage-clear summary screen: kills by enemy kind × points + survive bonus + running total
- Player keeps lives & score across stages; lose-all-lives or eagle-hit ends the run
- "Best score" + "Top stage reached" persisted via useHighScore

Tank-vs-tank collision (was ghost-mode)
- tryMove now takes a `others` list and rejects moves that overlap any live tank
- Player blocked by enemies; enemies blocked by player + each other
- Stuck enemies redirect quickly (aiTimer drops to 120ms on blocked move)

Enemy variety
- 3 kinds: basic (1 hp, 100 pts), fast (1 hp, faster, 200 pts), armor (3 hp, slow, 400 pts)
- HP indicator dots on multi-hit tanks
- Per-kind colors: silver / white / gold

UI closer to historical Battle City
- Enemy queue strip above the field — one mini-tank icon per un-spawned enemy
- Title now includes current stage: "Tanks · Stage N"
- Stage-clear breakdown matches NES bookkeeping layout
- Bullets visually distinct (player/enemy)

Build single-player Riichi v0.2 engine + UI

Pure-TS engine under web/src/engine/:
- tiles.ts: 34-type tile system, Unicode glyphs, parseHand/formatHand helpers
- wall.ts: 136-tile shuffled wall + dead wall + dora indicator + deal
- evaluator.ts: 14-tile shape decomposer (standard / chiitoitsu / kokushi)
                with isTenpai and waits helpers
- yaku.ts: subset detector (Riichi, Ippatsu, Menzen Tsumo, Pinfu, Tanyao,
           Yakuhai for round/seat winds + dragons, Iipeikou, Toitoi,
           Honitsu, Chinitsu, Chiitoitsu, Kokushi)
- score.ts: naive fu (30 / 25 chiitoitsu) + han + base-point lookup with
            mangan/haneman/baiman/sanbaiman/yakuman caps; per-payer
            transfers with round-up-to-100
- game.ts: state machine for one kyoku — human seat 0 vs three random-
           discard bots, riichi/tsumo/ron actions for the human

UI under web/src/components/Board.tsx:
- Bottom row: 13-tile hand + drawn tile (lifted), tap to discard
- 3 opponents shown as tile-back rows (top/left/right)
- 4 discard piles in the centre of the table
- Riichi / Tsumo / Ron buttons surface only when legal
- Win modal with yaku list, han/fu, points, and the round's score table

v0.2 cuts (documented in App.tsx rules popover):
- No calling chi/pon/kan — fully closed hands only
- Bots never call, riichi, or tsumo
- Single hand per session, no honba/round progression
- Fixed fu (30 standard, 25 chiitoitsu)
- Rare yaku (sanshoku/ittsuu/chanta/haitei/rinshan/etc.) not detected
- Multiplayer over FGS rooms is planned but not implemented

16 tests pass (12 evaluator + 4 scoring integration).
